title: Website Code Audit Guide: How to Review, Fix, and Improve Your Website Code
excerpt: Learn how to perform a complete website code audit for performance, SEO, accessibility, security, JavaScript rendering, Core Web Vitals, structured data, and maintainability.
author: DevelopersMatrix Editorial Team
content:
## Quick Answer

A website code audit is a structured review of a website's front-end code, back-end logic, SEO implementation, performance, accessibility, security, and maintainability. The goal is to find issues that hurt speed, search visibility, user experience, conversion rate, scalability, and long-term development efficiency.

A strong audit checks HTML, CSS, JavaScript, server responses, Core Web Vitals, structured data, crawlability, accessibility, security risks, third-party scripts, and code quality. The result should be a prioritized action plan that separates critical technical problems from lower-priority improvements.

> **Related:** Want to audit your website instantly? Try our free [Website Audit Tool](/tools/website-audit) — checks SEO, speed, mobile UX, and security in 60 seconds.

## Table of Contents

- What Is a Website Code Audit?
- Why Website Code Audits Matter
- Website Code Audit vs SEO Audit vs Performance Audit
- When Should You Run a Website Code Audit?
- What Should a Website Code Audit Include?
- Step 1: Crawl the Website
- Step 2: Audit HTML Structure
- Step 3: Review CSS Quality and Layout Stability
- Step 4: Audit JavaScript Performance and Rendering
- Step 5: Audit Core Web Vitals
- Step 6: Audit Technical SEO Code
- Step 7: Audit Structured Data
- Step 8: Audit Accessibility
- Step 9: Audit Security Risks
- Step 10: Audit Images and Media
- Step 11: Audit Third-Party Scripts
- Step 12: Audit Code Maintainability
- Website Code Audit Tools
- Website Code Audit Priority Matrix
- Code Audit Checklist for Developers
- Frequently Asked Questions

## What Is a Website Code Audit?

A website code audit is a detailed inspection of the code and technical systems that power a website. It identifies problems that may not be visible on the surface but can affect how users, search engines, browsers, and development teams experience the site.

A normal website review may focus on appearance, design, or content. A code audit goes deeper. It examines how the website is built, loaded, rendered, indexed, secured, and maintained.

A complete website code audit usually includes:

- HTML validation
- CSS quality
- JavaScript performance
- Core Web Vitals
- Mobile responsiveness
- Technical SEO
- Accessibility
- Security risks
- Structured data
- Crawlability
- Indexability
- Redirect behavior
- Image optimization
- Server response codes
- Third-party scripts
- Code maintainability
- CMS or framework implementation

For business websites, SaaS platforms, eCommerce stores, agencies, and content-heavy websites, code quality directly affects revenue. Slow pages reduce conversions. Broken markup can damage usability. Poor JavaScript rendering can block search engines. Security weaknesses can expose customer data. Accessibility issues can prevent users from completing important actions.

> **Related:** Looking for a complete technical review? Our free [Website Audit Tool](/tools/website-audit) runs 260+ checks including all the areas covered in this guide.

A website code audit helps prevent these problems before they become expensive.

## Why Website Code Audits Matter

Modern websites are no longer simple static pages. They often include JavaScript frameworks, CMS templates, analytics scripts, tracking pixels, personalization tools, plugins, APIs, payment systems, forms, and third-party integrations.

Every layer introduces risk.

A website may look good visually while still having serious technical problems, such as:

- Pages that load slowly on mobile devices
- Render-blocking JavaScript
- Invalid HTML structure
- Missing alt text
- Duplicate meta tags
- Broken canonical tags
- Bloated CSS files
- Unused JavaScript bundles
- Poor heading hierarchy
- Insecure forms
- Accessibility barriers
- Missing structured data
- Crawl traps
- 404 errors
- Redirect chains
- Poor caching rules

Search engines increasingly evaluate technical quality, user experience, and page performance. Google describes Core Web Vitals as metrics that measure real-world user experience for loading performance, interactivity, and visual stability, and recommends achieving good scores for Search and user experience generally.

A code audit is not only for developers. It helps marketers, founders, SEO teams, product managers, and business owners understand what is holding a website back.

## Website Code Audit vs SEO Audit vs Performance Audit

A website code audit overlaps with SEO and performance audits, but it is broader.

| Audit Type | Main Focus | What It Checks |
|---|---|---|
| Website Code Audit | Technical foundation | HTML, CSS, JavaScript, architecture, accessibility, SEO, security, performance |
| SEO Audit | Search visibility | Crawlability, indexing, metadata, content, internal links, structured data |
| Performance Audit | Speed and responsiveness | Core Web Vitals, scripts, images, caching, server response time |
| Security Audit | Risk reduction | Authentication, input handling, headers, dependencies, exposed data |
| Accessibility Audit | Inclusive usability | Keyboard navigation, contrast, labels, semantic HTML, screen reader support |

The best approach is to combine these views into one technical roadmap.

> **Related:** Want a complete audit right now? Run our free [Website Audit Tool](/tools/website-audit) that checks SEO, performance, accessibility, and security.

## When Should You Run a Website Code Audit?

You should audit website code when:

- Launching a new website
- Redesigning an existing website
- Migrating to a new CMS or framework
- Experiencing traffic drops
- Seeing poor Core Web Vitals scores
- Adding major new features
- Preparing for SEO campaigns
- Before paid advertising campaigns
- After hiring a new development team
- Before selling or acquiring a website
- When conversion rates decline
- When security concerns appear

For active business websites, a light audit every quarter and a full technical audit once or twice per year is a practical rhythm.

For eCommerce, SaaS, and high-traffic websites, code audits should become part of the release process.

## What Should a Website Code Audit Include?

A complete website code audit should evaluate seven major areas:

| Audit Area | Why It Matters |
|---|---|
| HTML and structure | Helps browsers, users, and search engines understand the page |
| CSS and layout | Affects responsiveness, visual stability, maintainability, and UX |
| JavaScript | Impacts rendering, interactivity, crawlability, and speed |
| SEO implementation | Determines whether pages can be discovered, indexed, and ranked |
| Performance | Affects Core Web Vitals, conversions, and user satisfaction |
| Accessibility | Ensures all users can interact with the site |
| Security | Protects users, data, forms, sessions, and business reputation |

Each area should be reviewed both manually and with tools. Automated tools are useful, but they cannot fully replace human judgment.

## Step 1: Crawl the Website

Start by crawling the website to understand its technical structure.

A crawl helps identify:

- Indexable pages
- Non-indexable pages
- Redirects
- Broken URLs
- Duplicate title tags
- Duplicate meta descriptions
- Missing canonical tags
- Orphan pages
- Thin pages
- Pagination issues
- Status code problems
- Internal linking gaps

Important status codes to review:

| Status Code | Meaning | Audit Action |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Page loads successfully | Confirm indexability and content quality |
| 301 | Permanent redirect | Check whether redirect is intentional |
| 302 | Temporary redirect | Confirm temporary use is correct |
| 404 | Page not found | Fix, redirect, or remove internal links |
| 410 | Gone | Use only when content is intentionally removed |
| 500 | Server error | Escalate immediately |
| 503 | Service unavailable | Confirm maintenance or server issue |

A crawl gives you the map before you inspect the code in detail.

## Step 2: Audit HTML Structure

HTML is the foundation of every web page. Clean, semantic HTML improves accessibility, SEO, rendering consistency, and long-term maintainability.

Review these elements:

- One clear h1 per page
- Logical heading hierarchy
- Descriptive title tag
- Unique meta description
- Correct canonical tag
- Semantic landmarks such as header, main, nav, section, and footer
- Valid form labels
- Proper button and link usage
- Descriptive alt text for meaningful images
- No duplicate IDs
- Clean list and table markup
- No unnecessary nested elements

The W3C Markup Validation Service checks the markup validity of web documents including HTML and XHTML. Validation does not guarantee a perfect website, but it is a useful way to catch syntax errors, unclosed tags, invalid nesting, and markup problems that can create rendering or accessibility issues.

### HTML Audit Checklist

| Check | Good Practice |
|---|---|
| Title tag | Unique, descriptive, keyword-relevant |
| Meta description | Unique and aligned with page intent |
| H1 | One primary H1 matching the page topic |
| Headings | Logical H2/H3 structure |
| Images | Relevant alt text where needed |
| Forms | Inputs connected to labels |
| Buttons | Used for actions, not navigation |
| Links | Used for navigation, not JavaScript-only actions |
| Tables | Use headers for data tables |
| Language | Add correct lang attribute |

## Step 3: Review CSS Quality and Layout Stability

CSS problems often show up as inconsistent layouts, mobile issues, overlapping elements, unnecessary complexity, and layout shifts.

During a CSS audit, review:

- Unused CSS
- Duplicate rules
- Overly specific selectors
- Large CSS files
- Render-blocking stylesheets
- Mobile breakpoints
- Layout shifts
- Font loading behavior
- Dark mode compatibility
- Print styles if relevant
- Component consistency
- CSS variables and design tokens

Poor CSS architecture makes websites difficult to maintain. A small design change can accidentally break many pages when styles are duplicated or written without structure.

### Common CSS Code Problems

| CSS Problem | Impact |
|---|---|
| Unused CSS | Increases file size and load time |
| Excessive specificity | Makes future updates difficult |
| Inline styles everywhere | Reduces maintainability |
| No responsive breakpoints | Hurts mobile experience |
| Missing image dimensions | Causes layout shift |
| Web fonts not optimized | Slows rendering |
| Inconsistent spacing | Weakens design quality |

### CSS Audit Tip

Look for repeated patterns. If the same button, card, grid, or section style appears in many different forms, the codebase may need reusable components.

## Step 4: Audit JavaScript Performance and Rendering

JavaScript is one of the most common causes of slow websites. It can delay rendering, block interactivity, increase bundle size, and create SEO problems when important content depends entirely on client-side rendering.

Google's JavaScript SEO documentation explains how Google processes JavaScript and provides best practices for making JavaScript-powered websites accessible to Google Search.

During a JavaScript audit, review:

- Bundle size
- Unused JavaScript
- Render-blocking scripts
- Third-party scripts
- Hydration cost
- Client-side rendering issues
- Lazy loading behavior
- Error logs
- Long tasks
- Event listener performance
- Framework configuration
- API dependency failures

### JavaScript Audit Checklist

| Check | What to Look For |
|---|---|
| Bundle size | Large JS files slowing load time |
| Unused JS | Code loaded but not used on the page |
| Third-party scripts | Analytics, chat widgets, pixels, ads, embeds |
| Rendering | Important content visible without excessive delay |
| Errors | Console errors and failed network requests |
| Long tasks | Main-thread blocking issues |
| Lazy loading | Applied to non-critical resources only |
| Code splitting | Load only what the page needs |

### JavaScript SEO Issues to Watch

JavaScript-heavy websites can create SEO problems when:

- Content appears only after delayed rendering
- Internal links are generated in non-crawlable ways
- Metadata changes after initial load
- Structured data is injected incorrectly
- Canonical tags are handled inconsistently
- Pages depend on blocked resources
- Infinite scroll lacks crawlable URLs

Google states that dynamic rendering is a workaround for sites where JavaScript-generated content is not available to search engines, but it is not a recommended long-term solution because it adds complexity and resource requirements.

For most modern projects, server-side rendering, static generation, or hybrid rendering is a better approach when SEO matters.

> **Related:** Check if your JavaScript is blocking search engines. Run our [free Website Audit](/tools/website-audit) — it includes JavaScript rendering checks.

## Step 5: Audit Core Web Vitals

Core Web Vitals are essential performance metrics that evaluate user experience. PageSpeed Insights identifies Core Web Vitals as INP, LCP, and CLS, and explains that passing requires all three metrics to be in the Good range at the 75th percentile where sufficient data is available.

The three Core Web Vitals are:

| Metric | What It Measures | Why It Matters |
|---|---|---|
| LCP | Loading performance | Measures when the main content becomes visible |
| INP | Interactivity | Measures responsiveness after user interactions |
| CLS | Visual stability | Measures unexpected layout shifts |

### Largest Contentful Paint Audit

LCP issues often come from:

- Slow server response times
- Large hero images
- Render-blocking CSS
- Render-blocking JavaScript
- Unoptimized fonts
- No caching
- Poor CDN configuration

Fixes may include:

- Compressing hero images
- Serving modern image formats
- Preloading critical assets
- Reducing server response time
- Removing render-blocking resources
- Using efficient caching
- Delivering assets through a CDN

### Interaction to Next Paint Audit

INP issues often come from:

- Heavy JavaScript execution
- Long main-thread tasks
- Large frameworks
- Inefficient event handlers
- Too many third-party scripts
- Complex DOM updates

Fixes may include:

- Reducing JavaScript bundle size
- Splitting long tasks
- Deferring non-critical scripts
- Removing unnecessary third-party tools
- Optimizing event handlers
- Simplifying client-side rendering

### Cumulative Layout Shift Audit

CLS issues often come from:

- Images without dimensions
- Ads or embeds loading late
- Fonts swapping unexpectedly
- Dynamic banners
- Injected content above existing content
- Sticky headers changing size

Fixes may include:

- Adding width and height to images
- Reserving space for ads and embeds
- Optimizing font loading
- Avoiding layout changes after load
- Using stable component dimensions

> **Related:** Check your Core Web Vitals scores instantly. Run our [free Website Audit](/tools/website-audit).

## Step 6: Audit Technical SEO Code

Technical SEO depends heavily on correct code implementation. A website can have strong content but still underperform if the code prevents search engines from crawling, rendering, or indexing pages properly.

Review:

- Title tags
- Meta descriptions
- Canonical tags
- Robots meta tags
- Robots.txt rules
- XML sitemap
- Structured data
- Heading structure
- Pagination
- Hreflang where relevant
- Open Graph tags
- Twitter/X card tags
- Mobile rendering
- Internal link markup
- JavaScript-generated links

### Technical SEO Code Checklist

| Element | Audit Question |
|---|---|
| Title tag | Is it unique, descriptive, and relevant? |
| Meta description | Does it match search intent? |
| Canonical tag | Does it point to the correct URL? |
| Robots meta | Is the page accidentally noindexed? |
| Sitemap | Are important pages included? |
| Robots.txt | Are important resources blocked? |
| Structured data | Is schema valid and relevant? |
| Internal links | Are links crawlable and meaningful? |
| Images | Are alt attributes useful? |
| Pagination | Can search engines follow page relationships? |

## Step 7: Audit Structured Data

Structured data helps search engines understand the content and context of a page. Google explains that structured data markup can help Google understand page content and may be used for rich results when eligible.

For a website code audit, check whether structured data is:

- Relevant to the page
- Valid JSON-LD
- Free from syntax errors
- Consistent with visible content
- Not misleading
- Not duplicated unnecessarily
- Implemented at template level where appropriate

Common schema types include:

| Page Type | Recommended Schema |
|---|---|
| Blog post | Article or BlogPosting |
| FAQ page | FAQPage |
| Product page | Product |
| Local business page | LocalBusiness |
| Service page | Service |
| How-to content | HowTo |
| Breadcrumbs | BreadcrumbList |
| Organization page | Organization |

### Structured Data Mistakes

Avoid these problems:

- Adding FAQ schema to pages without visible FAQs
- Marking up fake reviews
- Duplicating schema across unrelated pages
- Injecting schema too late with JavaScript
- Using invalid JSON syntax
- Using outdated or irrelevant schema types

## Step 8: Audit Accessibility

Accessibility ensures that people with different abilities can use your website. It also improves usability for everyone.

A code audit should review:

- Keyboard navigation
- Focus states
- Color contrast
- ARIA usage
- Form labels
- Error messages
- Heading hierarchy
- Semantic landmarks
- Image alt text
- Button names
- Skip links
- Screen reader compatibility

The W3C develops standards and guidelines to help build a web based on accessibility, internationalization, privacy, and security principles. Accessibility should not be treated as a final QA task. It should be part of the design and development process from the beginning.

### Accessibility Audit Table

| Issue | Why It Matters |
|---|---|
| Missing form labels | Screen reader users may not understand inputs |
| Poor contrast | Text becomes difficult to read |
| No keyboard support | Users cannot navigate without a mouse |
| Incorrect ARIA | Assistive technology receives wrong information |
| Missing focus style | Keyboard users lose track of position |
| Empty buttons | Users do not know what the action does |
| Poor heading order | Page structure becomes confusing |

## Step 9: Audit Security Risks

Security is a critical part of a website code audit. Even marketing websites can expose risks through forms, outdated plugins, third-party scripts, weak headers, or vulnerable dependencies.

OWASP describes the OWASP Top 10 as a standard awareness document for developers and web application security that represents a broad consensus about critical web application security risks. The most current released version is the OWASP Top 10 2025.

Security checks should include:

- HTTPS enforcement
- Secure cookies
- Content Security Policy
- Input validation
- Output encoding
- Dependency vulnerabilities
- Authentication flow
- Authorization logic
- Exposed API keys
- Sensitive data in source code
- Form spam protection
- File upload restrictions
- Security headers
- Admin panel exposure

### Security Header Checklist

| Header | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Content-Security-Policy | Reduces risk from malicious script injection |
| Strict-Transport-Security | Enforces HTTPS |
| X-Content-Type-Options | Helps prevent MIME sniffing |
| Referrer-Policy | Controls referrer information |
| Permissions-Policy | Limits browser feature access |
| X-Frame-Options | Helps prevent clickjacking |

### Common Website Security Problems

| Problem | Risk |
|---|---|
| Outdated dependencies | Known vulnerabilities |
| Weak form validation | Spam or injection attacks |
| Exposed secrets | API abuse or data leaks |
| Missing HTTPS redirects | Insecure traffic |
| Overly permissive CORS | Unauthorized access risks |
| No rate limiting | Abuse and brute force attempts |
| Weak admin passwords | Account takeover |

> **Related:** Check your website security instantly. Our [free Website Audit](/tools/website-audit) includes security checks.

## Step 10: Audit Images and Media

Images are often the largest assets on a page. Poor image handling can hurt speed, layout stability, accessibility, and mobile experience.

Review:

- Image file sizes
- Image dimensions
- Responsive images
- Lazy loading
- Modern formats
- Alt text
- Background images
- Video embeds
- Autoplay behavior
- CDN delivery

### Image Audit Checklist

| Check | Recommended Action |
|---|---|
| Large images | Compress and resize |
| Missing dimensions | Add width and height |
| Non-responsive images | Use responsive image techniques |
| Decorative images | Use empty alt text where appropriate |
| Important images | Add descriptive alt text |
| Hero image | Preload when it is the LCP element |
| Videos | Avoid autoplay with sound |

## Step 11: Audit Third-Party Scripts

Third-party scripts can quietly slow a website more than the site's own code. These include analytics tools, tracking pixels, heatmaps, chat widgets, review widgets, A/B testing platforms, advertising scripts, and embeds.

Audit each script by asking:

- Is this script still needed?
- Who owns it?
- What pages require it?
- Does it block rendering?
- Does it affect Core Web Vitals?
- Does it collect user data?
- Is it loaded before consent where consent is required?
- Can it be delayed, deferred, or loaded conditionally?

### Third-Party Script Priority Table

| Script Type | Risk Level | Audit Action |
|---|---|---|
| Payment scripts | High importance | Keep, but load securely |
| Analytics | Medium | Keep only necessary tools |
| Chat widgets | Medium to high | Delay or conditionally load |
| Heatmaps | Medium | Use only during testing windows |
| Ads | High performance impact | Reserve layout space and monitor CLS |
| Social embeds | Medium | Lazy load where possible |
| Unused pixels | Low value, high clutter | Remove |

## Step 12: Audit Code Maintainability

A website that works today can become expensive tomorrow if the code is difficult to maintain.

Maintainability issues include:

- Repeated components
- No naming conventions
- Hard-coded values
- Inline CSS and JavaScript
- Large unorganized files
- No documentation
- No version control discipline
- Plugin conflicts
- Unclear template hierarchy
- Poor separation of concerns

### Maintainability Audit Questions

Ask these questions during the review:

1. Can a developer understand the structure quickly?
2. Are components reusable?
3. Are styles organized logically?
4. Is JavaScript modular?
5. Are dependencies documented?
6. Are build tools configured correctly?
7. Are environment variables handled safely?
8. Are templates easy to update?
9. Is there a rollback process?
10. Are critical functions tested?

A maintainable codebase reduces future development cost and lowers the risk of accidental breakage.

## Website Code Audit Tools

A professional website code audit usually uses several tools instead of relying on one platform.

| Tool Category | Examples of What It Helps With |
|---|---|
| Browser DevTools | Console errors, network requests, layout shifts, performance profiling |
| PageSpeed Insights | Core Web Vitals and performance recommendations |
| Lighthouse | Performance, accessibility, SEO, best practices |
| W3C Validator | HTML validation |
| Search Console | Indexing, crawling, Core Web Vitals, search performance |
| Screaming Frog or Sitebulb | Crawling, metadata, status codes, internal links |
| Security scanners | Headers, dependency risks, exposed vulnerabilities |
| Accessibility tools | Contrast, labels, ARIA, keyboard issues |
| Code linters | Syntax, formatting, code quality |
| Bundle analyzers | JavaScript bundle size and unused code |

> **Related:** Get all these checks in one place. Our [free Website Audit Tool](/tools/website-audit) runs 260+ automated checks covering every area in this guide.

Tools identify symptoms. The audit report should explain causes and solutions.

## Website Code Audit Priority Matrix

Not every issue has the same urgency. A good audit separates critical fixes from nice-to-have improvements.

| Priority | Issue Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | Breaks indexing, security, checkout, forms, or page access | Important pages accidentally noindexed |
| High | Strong impact on SEO, speed, UX, or revenue | Poor LCP on main landing pages |
| Medium | Noticeable but not business-critical | Duplicate meta descriptions on low-priority pages |
| Low | Cleanup or future improvement | Minor CSS refactoring |

### Recommended Fix Order

1. Security issues
2. Broken pages and server errors
3. Indexing and crawlability problems
4. Critical Core Web Vitals issues
5. Mobile usability problems
6. Accessibility blockers
7. Structured data errors
8. Code cleanup
9. UX polish
10. Documentation improvements

## Code Audit Checklist for Developers

Use this checklist during a manual audit:

- [ ] Validate HTML structure
- [ ] Check heading hierarchy
- [ ] Review title and meta tags
- [ ] Confirm canonical tags
- [ ] Inspect robots meta tags
- [ ] Review sitemap and robots.txt
- [ ] Test mobile responsiveness
- [ ] Check Core Web Vitals
- [ ] Review JavaScript bundle size
- [ ] Remove unused scripts
- [ ] Audit third-party tools
- [ ] Check console errors
- [ ] Inspect network requests
- [ ] Review image sizes
- [ ] Add image dimensions
- [ ] Test keyboard navigation
- [ ] Check form labels
- [ ] Test color contrast
- [ ] Validate structured data
- [ ] Review security headers
- [ ] Check dependencies
- [ ] Review redirects
- [ ] Fix broken links
- [ ] Document findings
- [ ] Prioritize fixes

## Common Website Code Audit Mistakes

### Mistake 1: Only Running Automated Tools

Automated tools are useful, but they miss context. A tool may flag a minor issue while ignoring a business-critical problem in a checkout flow or lead form.

### Mistake 2: Ignoring Mobile Performance

Many websites perform acceptably on desktop but poorly on mobile. Since users often browse on mobile devices and mobile networks vary widely, mobile performance must be reviewed carefully.

### Mistake 3: Treating SEO and Code Separately

SEO problems often come from code. Canonicals, headings, schema, internal links, rendering, and indexability all depend on implementation.

### Mistake 4: Fixing Low-Impact Issues First

Teams often spend time on cosmetic cleanup while ignoring high-impact speed, security, or indexing problems.

### Mistake 5: Not Rechecking After Fixes

Every fix should be verified. A resolved issue can create a new issue if changes are deployed without testing.

## How Often Should You Audit Website Code?

Recommended audit frequency depends on website complexity.

| Website Type | Recommended Frequency |
|---|---|
| Small business website | Every 6-12 months |
| Blog or content website | Every 3-6 months |
| eCommerce website | Quarterly |
| SaaS website | Quarterly or per major release |
| Enterprise website | Monthly technical monitoring plus deep audits |
| High-traffic website | Continuous monitoring |

A full audit may not be required every month, but key health checks should be monitored consistently.

> **Related:** Want continuous monitoring? Run our [free Website Audit](/tools/website-audit) anytime to check your website health.

## Key Takeaways

- A website code audit reviews the technical foundation of a website.
- Code quality affects SEO, speed, accessibility, security, conversions, and maintenance cost.
- Core Web Vitals should be part of every audit.
- JavaScript rendering must be reviewed carefully for SEO and performance.
- Accessibility and security should not be optional.
- Automated tools help, but manual review is still necessary.
- The final audit report should prioritize fixes by business impact.

> **Ready to audit your website?** [Run our free Website Audit Tool](/tools/website-audit) and get 260+ checks on SEO, speed, security, accessibility, and mobile performance — in 60 seconds.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is a website code audit?

A website code audit is a technical review of a website's HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SEO implementation, performance, accessibility, security, and maintainability. It identifies issues that affect user experience, search visibility, and long-term development quality.

### Why is a website code audit important?

A code audit helps find hidden technical issues that can slow the website, block search engines, reduce conversions, create accessibility barriers, or introduce security risks.

### How long does a website code audit take?

A small website may take a few hours to audit, while a large eCommerce or SaaS website can take several days or weeks depending on complexity, page count, integrations, and reporting depth.

### What tools are used for a website code audit?

Common tools include browser DevTools, PageSpeed Insights, Lighthouse, Google Search Console, W3C Validator, crawling tools, accessibility checkers, security scanners, and JavaScript bundle analyzers.

### Is a code audit the same as an SEO audit?

No. An SEO audit focuses on search visibility, while a code audit reviews the broader technical foundation. However, many SEO problems are caused by code implementation issues.

### Can poor code hurt Google rankings?

Yes. Poor code can affect crawlability, indexability, structured data, mobile usability, page speed, and user experience. These factors can influence search performance.

### What are Core Web Vitals?

Core Web Vitals are performance metrics that evaluate loading speed, interactivity, and visual stability. The current Core Web Vitals are LCP, INP, and CLS.

### How do I audit JavaScript SEO?

Check whether important content, links, metadata, canonical tags, and structured data are available to search engines after rendering. Review JavaScript errors, delayed content, blocked resources, and client-side routing.

### What is the most common website code audit issue?

Common issues include large images, unused JavaScript, render-blocking resources, missing metadata, invalid HTML, accessibility problems, and too many third-party scripts.

### Should every website use structured data?

Not every page needs structured data, but many page types benefit from relevant schema markup. Blog posts, products, FAQs, breadcrumbs, services, and organization pages often use structured data.

### How often should I run a website code audit?

Most business websites should run a full audit every 6-12 months. High-traffic, eCommerce, and SaaS websites should audit more frequently, especially after major updates.

### What should be included in a website code audit report?

A good report includes an executive summary, issue list, affected URLs, screenshots or evidence, business impact, recommended fixes, priority level, estimated effort, and owner assignment.

### Can I do a code audit without being a developer?

You can perform a basic audit using tools, but deeper issues involving JavaScript, rendering, security, and architecture usually require development expertise.

### What is the first thing to check in a code audit?

Start with crawlability, indexing status, server errors, HTTPS, and major performance problems. These issues often have the highest business impact.

### What is the difference between validation and audit?

Validation checks whether code follows certain syntax or standards. An audit evaluates whether the website is technically effective, accessible, secure, fast, and maintainable.

title: How Does the TikTok Algorithm Work in 2026? Complete Creator Guide to More Views and Engagement

author: DevelopersMatrix Editorial Team
content:
## Quick Answer

The TikTok algorithm in 2026 recommends videos based on viewer satisfaction signals such as watch time, completion rate, replays, shares, saves, comments, search relevance, and user interests. The platform does not rely only on follower count. Instead, it tests content with relevant audiences, measures how people respond, and expands reach when a video proves it can hold attention and create meaningful engagement.

For creators, brands, agencies, and businesses, the practical lesson is simple: TikTok growth depends on creating content that people watch, finish, search for, save, share, and discuss.

> **Related:** Want to understand how algorithms shape all social platforms? Read our complete guide on the [TikTok Algorithm 2026](/trends/tiktok-algorithm-2026-complete-guide) trend analysis.

## Table of Contents

- What Is the TikTok Algorithm?
- Why the TikTok Algorithm Matters in 2026
- How TikTok Distributes Videos
- TikTok Ranking Factors in 2026
- TikTok SEO in 2026
- TikTok SEO vs Google SEO
- The RISE Framework for TikTok Growth
- Common TikTok Algorithm Mistakes
- TikTok Algorithm Myths
- Best TikTok Growth Strategy for 2026
- Frequently Asked Questions

## What Is the TikTok Algorithm?

The TikTok algorithm is an AI-powered recommendation system that decides which videos appear on each user's For You Page, also known as the FYP. Every user receives a personalized feed based on what they watch, skip, like, comment on, save, share, search for, and engage with over time.

Unlike older social platforms that heavily depend on who a user follows, TikTok focuses on content discovery. This means a video from a new creator can appear next to content from a major influencer if the system believes the video is relevant and engaging for a particular viewer.

The algorithm evaluates three broad categories of signals:

| Signal Category | What It Includes | Why It Matters |
|---|---|---|
| User behavior | Watch time, skips, likes, comments, saves, shares, follows, searches | Shows what each user enjoys |
| Video information | Captions, hashtags, sounds, spoken words, on-screen text, topic, niche | Helps TikTok understand the content |
| Account and device context | Language preference, location signals, device settings, category interest | Helps improve relevance |

This personalization is why two users can open TikTok at the same time and see completely different videos. Their feeds are shaped by their behavior, interests, and interaction history.

## Why the TikTok Algorithm Matters in 2026

Understanding the TikTok algorithm matters because organic reach is no longer based only on posting frequently or using trending sounds. In 2026, creators need to understand how the recommendation engine evaluates quality, relevance, and viewer satisfaction.

A creator who understands the algorithm can:

- Increase video views without relying only on paid ads
- Build topical authority in a niche
- Improve retention and completion rate
- Create search-friendly videos that continue getting discovered
- Turn casual viewers into followers
- Increase saves, shares, and meaningful comments
- Build long-term visibility instead of short viral spikes

For businesses, TikTok is also a discovery platform. Users search for product reviews, tutorials, local recommendations, software tools, marketing tips, career advice, and step-by-step solutions. That means TikTok content can influence awareness, trust, and purchase decisions.

> **Related:** Running a business website? Get discovered faster with our free [Website Audit Tool](/tools/website-audit) — check your SEO, speed, and mobile performance.

The most successful TikTok strategies in 2026 combine creativity, retention, search optimization, and audience understanding.

## How TikTok Distributes Videos

TikTok usually distributes videos through a staged testing process. While the exact system is not publicly visible, creators can understand the process through performance patterns.

| Stage | What Happens | Main Signals Measured |
|---|---|---|
| Initial Test | The video is shown to a small relevant audience | Swipe rate, early watch time, first engagement |
| Evaluation | TikTok measures whether viewers continue watching | Completion rate, average watch duration, replays |
| Expansion | The video reaches larger groups with similar interests | Shares, saves, comments, retention consistency |
| Scaling | TikTok increases distribution if performance remains strong | Topic fit, engagement quality, session contribution |
| Long-Tail Discovery | The video may keep gaining views through search or recommendations | Search relevance, evergreen value, repeated engagement |

### Stage 1: Initial Testing

When a new video is published, TikTok does not immediately show it to everyone. Instead, it starts by testing the video with a limited group of users who may be interested in that type of content.

During this first phase, TikTok watches for immediate signals:

- Do viewers stop scrolling?
- Do they watch past the first few seconds?
- Do they finish the video?
- Do they replay it?
- Do they interact with it?
- Do they swipe away quickly?

A weak opening can stop growth before the video gets a larger test. This is why the first few seconds matter so much.

### Stage 2: Evaluation

After the initial test, TikTok compares the video's performance against other content in similar categories. A comedy video is not evaluated the same way as a detailed tutorial. A 12-second clip is not measured exactly like a 3-minute educational breakdown.

The system looks for performance relative to content type, audience expectation, and topic.

Strong evaluation signals include:

- High completion rate
- Strong average watch duration
- Replays from the same viewers
- Comments that show real interest
- Saves for future reference
- Shares to friends or groups
- Profile visits after watching

### Stage 3: Expansion

If a video performs well in testing, TikTok expands it to a larger audience. This new audience is usually similar to the users who responded positively during the first test.

For example, if a video about TikTok SEO tips for small businesses performs well with marketers, creators, and agency owners, TikTok may continue showing it to users who watch marketing, social media, and business growth content.

### Stage 4: Scaling

During the scaling phase, the video may receive thousands, hundreds of thousands, or even millions of views. This happens when retention and engagement remain strong across multiple audience groups.

However, scaling can stop quickly if the video performs well with one group but poorly with another. TikTok continues measuring satisfaction at every level.

### Stage 5: Long-Tail Discovery

Not every successful video goes viral immediately. Some videos grow slowly through TikTok search, related content recommendations, and niche interest signals.

Evergreen educational content can continue gaining views days, weeks, or months after publication if it answers a clear question or solves a recurring problem.

## How the TikTok Algorithm Has Changed

TikTok has evolved from a trend-focused entertainment platform into a search-driven discovery engine.

| Year | Major Algorithm Shift |
|---|---|
| 2020 | Engagement signals became central to distribution |
| 2021 | Watch time and completion rate gained stronger influence |
| 2022 | Search behavior became more important |
| 2023 | TikTok SEO became a serious creator growth strategy |
| 2024 | Topic authority and niche consistency became more valuable |
| 2025 | AI content classification and intent matching improved |
| 2026 | Viewer intent, search relevance, and satisfaction signals dominate |

The biggest shift in 2026 is intent-based discovery. TikTok is not only asking, What does this user watch? It is also trying to understand, What does this user want right now?

That change matters because creators can no longer depend only on viral formats. They need to create content that clearly serves a viewer need.

## TikTok Ranking Factors in 2026

TikTok uses many ranking signals, but some matter more than others. The strongest signals usually relate to retention, satisfaction, relevance, and engagement quality.

## TikTok Ranking Factors Comparison Table

| Ranking Factor | Importance | Impact on Reach | Creator Action |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Watch Time | Very High | Extremely Strong | Keep videos focused and engaging |
| Completion Rate | Very High | Extremely Strong | Deliver value quickly and clearly |
| Replays | High | Strong | Add surprising, useful, or dense moments |
| Shares | High | Strong | Create relatable or highly useful content |
| Saves | High | Strong | Make tutorials, checklists, and reference content |
| Search Relevance | High | Strong | Use keywords in speech, captions, and text |
| Topic Authority | High | Strong | Publish consistently within a niche |
| Comments | Medium | Moderate | Ask specific discussion-based questions |
| Likes | Medium | Moderate | Useful, but weaker than saves or shares |
| Hashtags | Low to Medium | Limited Alone | Use relevant tags, not random viral tags |
| Followers | Low | Minimal Alone | Helpful for trust, not the main reach driver |

## 1. Watch Time

Watch time is one of the most important TikTok ranking factors. If viewers stay with your video, TikTok sees that as a positive signal.

Watch time is not only about video length. A short video with excellent retention can outperform a long video with poor retention. Likewise, a long video can perform well if viewers stay engaged throughout.

To improve watch time:

- Start with the result, problem, or promise immediately
- Remove unnecessary intros
- Use fast pacing without making the video confusing
- Add visual changes every few seconds
- Keep each sentence useful
- Avoid repeating the same idea
- Use curiosity loops to hold attention

Example:

Weak opening: Hey guys, today I want to talk about TikTok.

Strong opening: Most TikTok videos fail in the first three seconds because creators make this mistake.

The second opening gives users a reason to stay.

## 2. Completion Rate

Completion rate measures how many viewers watch your video until the end. It is especially important for short-form videos because TikTok can quickly determine whether the content delivered on its promise.

A high completion rate tells the algorithm that viewers found the content worth finishing.

Ways to increase completion rate:

- Make the video shorter if the idea is simple
- Avoid slow introductions
- Promise a clear payoff
- Structure the video with a beginning, middle, and end
- Use captions or on-screen text to support the message
- End with a useful conclusion instead of fading out

For short videos, creators should aim for a very high completion rate. For longer videos, average watch duration becomes equally important.

## 3. Replays

Replays occur when a viewer watches the same video more than once. This is a powerful signal because it shows that the content was interesting, entertaining, useful, surprising, or information-dense enough to watch again.

Common replay triggers include:

- Fast tutorials
- Before-and-after results
- Surprising reveals
- Step-by-step breakdowns
- Funny moments
- Data-packed explanations
- Content with hidden details

A simple way to encourage replays is to provide value in a compact format. If a viewer thinks, I need to watch that again, the video sends a strong quality signal.

## 4. Shares

Shares are stronger than likes because they require more effort. When users share a video, they are telling TikTok that the content is worth sending to another person.

Shareable content usually has one of these qualities:

- It is highly relatable
- It solves a specific problem
- It teaches something useful
- It expresses a belief people agree with
- It is funny enough to send to friends
- It helps someone make a decision
- It explains something complex in a simple way

For brands, shares are especially valuable because they expand reach beyond the original viewer.

## 5. Saves

Saves are a strong signal for educational, tutorial, checklist, and reference content. When users save a video, they are saying the content has future value.

Content that earns saves often includes:

- Step-by-step tutorials
- Tool lists
- Marketing checklists
- Fitness routines
- Recipes
- Templates
- Business tips
- Coding shortcuts
- Product recommendations

To increase saves, make your content practical. A video titled 5 TikTok SEO checks before posting is more save-worthy than a vague video titled TikTok growth tips.

## 6. Comments

Comments help TikTok measure engagement, but not all comments have the same value. Meaningful discussion is more useful than generic engagement bait.

For example, Comment YES if you agree may create activity, but it does not always create useful conversation. A stronger prompt would be:

What niche are you posting in, and what is your biggest TikTok growth problem right now?

That question invites detailed responses and gives the creator future content ideas.

## 7. Search Relevance

TikTok SEO is now an important part of growth. Videos can appear when users search for specific keywords, questions, products, or tutorials.

TikTok uses several signals to understand video topics:

- Spoken words
- Captions
- On-screen text
- Hashtags
- Sounds
- Visual context
- User engagement patterns
- Creator niche

If your video is about the TikTok algorithm, the phrase should appear naturally in your spoken audio, caption, and on-screen text.

## 8. Topic Authority

Topic authority means TikTok understands what your account is about. When you consistently publish around a specific niche, the platform has more confidence about which audience should see your content.

Example niche clusters:

| Broad Niche | Topic Cluster Examples |
|---|---|
| Social Media Marketing | TikTok SEO, Instagram growth, content strategy, analytics |
| Web Development | JavaScript tips, Shopify development, WordPress fixes, UI design |
| Fitness | Fat loss, strength training, meal prep, recovery |
| Business | Lead generation, sales scripts, productivity, branding |
| Education | Study tips, exam preparation, career advice, skill learning |

A random account that posts cooking, memes, business advice, travel, and fitness may confuse the recommendation system. A focused account gives TikTok clearer signals.

## 9. Viewer Satisfaction

Viewer satisfaction is broader than likes or comments. TikTok wants to know whether a video made the user happy, informed, entertained, or satisfied enough to continue using the platform.

Possible satisfaction signals include:

- The viewer watches until the end
- The viewer does not immediately swipe away
- The viewer follows the creator
- The viewer watches similar videos afterward
- The viewer saves or shares the content
- The viewer searches related topics

A video can get many views but still stop scaling if users do not appear satisfied after watching.

## 10. Session Contribution

Session contribution refers to how a video affects the user's overall TikTok session. If a video keeps people engaged and encourages continued platform use, it may receive stronger distribution.

This does not mean every video must be addictive or sensational. Useful content can contribute to a positive session if it leads users to watch more related content, follow the creator, or search for more information.

## TikTok SEO in 2026

TikTok SEO is the process of optimizing videos so TikTok can understand, categorize, and rank them for relevant searches and recommendations.

This matters because users increasingly search on TikTok for answers, tutorials, reviews, and recommendations.

Examples of TikTok searches include:

- How does the TikTok algorithm work?
- TikTok SEO tips
- Best AI tools for small business
- Shopify product page design
- How to edit videos faster
- Best laptop for developers
- Content ideas for real estate agents

If your video answers a specific search query clearly, it has a better chance of being discovered beyond the For You Page.

## TikTok SEO Checklist for 2026

| Optimization Area | What to Do | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Spoken keyword | Say the main keyword naturally | Here is how the TikTok algorithm works in 2026. |
| Caption | Add a clear keyword-rich caption | TikTok algorithm tips for more views in 2026. |
| On-screen text | Display the topic visually | TikTok Algorithm Ranking Factors |
| Hashtags | Use relevant hashtags | #TikTokSEO #TikTokAlgorithm #CreatorTips |
| Search intent | Match what users want | Explain, compare, review, or solve |
| Video structure | Deliver the answer quickly | Hook, value, example, takeaway |
| Engagement prompt | Ask a useful question | Which ranking factor do you struggle with most? |

## Where to Place TikTok Keywords

| Keyword Location | Importance | Best Practice |
|---|---:|---|
| Spoken audio | Very High | Say the target keyword in the first few seconds |
| On-screen text | High | Use a clear title or label |
| Caption | High | Write naturally, not keyword stuffing |
| Hashtags | Medium | Use specific, relevant hashtags |
| Profile bio | Medium | Reinforce niche authority |
| Username | Low | Helpful only if naturally branded |

A good TikTok SEO strategy does not mean repeating the same keyword too many times. It means making the topic clear to both users and the algorithm.

## TikTok SEO vs Google SEO

TikTok SEO and Google SEO share the same goal: helping users find useful content. However, they work differently.

| Factor | TikTok SEO | Google SEO |
|---|---|---|
| Main content format | Short-form and vertical video | Web pages, articles, videos, images |
| Ranking signal | Watch behavior and engagement | Relevance, authority, content quality |
| Keywords | Important in audio, captions, text | Important in title, headings, copy |
| Backlinks | Not a core TikTok factor | Major authority signal |
| Retention | Very important | Indirectly important |
| Freshness | Often important | Depends on query |
| Engagement | Strong signal | Usually less direct |
| Search intent | Very important | Very important |

For creators, the best approach is to combine both. A topic can become a TikTok video, a blog post, a YouTube video, and a social carousel. This creates a stronger content ecosystem.

## The RISE Framework for TikTok Growth

The RISE Framework is a simple way to understand TikTok growth in 2026.

RISE stands for:

- Retention
- Intent
- Shares
- Engagement

### R — Retention

Retention is the foundation. If viewers leave quickly, the algorithm has little reason to expand the video.

Improve retention by:

- Opening with a strong hook
- Cutting filler
- Using clear visuals
- Adding pattern interrupts
- Delivering value quickly
- Ending with a payoff

### I — Intent

Intent means understanding what the viewer wants. A video should match a specific need, question, emotion, or problem.

Examples:

| Viewer Intent | Video Idea |
|---|---|
| Learn | How TikTok ranks videos in 2026 |
| Compare | TikTok SEO vs Instagram SEO |
| Decide | Should your business post on TikTok? |
| Fix | Why your TikTok views are dropping |
| Improve | 3 ways to increase TikTok watch time |

### S — Shares

Shareable content spreads faster. It reaches not only the original viewer but also their network.

To create shareable content, ask:

- Would someone send this to a friend?
- Does this solve a common problem?
- Is it surprising or useful?
- Does it express something the audience already feels?
- Is it simple enough to understand quickly?

### E — Engagement

Engagement gives TikTok more context about content quality and audience interest.

Strong engagement is specific, not generic. Instead of asking people to comment randomly, invite them into a useful conversation.

Examples:

- What niche are you trying to grow on TikTok?
- Which part of TikTok SEO confuses you most?
- Do you get more views from search or the For You Page?
- What is your average completion rate?

## Best TikTok Content Types in 2026

Not all content types perform the same way. Some are better for reach, some are better for saves, and some are better for conversions.

| Content Type | Growth Potential | Best For |
|---|---:|---|
| Educational videos | Very High | Saves, search traffic, authority |
| Tutorials | Very High | Retention, saves, evergreen discovery |
| Product reviews | High | Search intent, purchase decisions |
| Storytelling | High | Watch time, emotional engagement |
| Case studies | High | Trust, authority, business audiences |
| Behind-the-scenes | Medium | Brand personality, connection |
| Trend-based videos | Medium | Short-term reach |
| Opinion content | Medium to High | Comments and discussion |
| Entertainment | High | Shares and replays |

Educational and tutorial content is especially powerful because it can perform on both the For You Page and TikTok Search.

## Best TikTok Growth Strategy for 2026

The best TikTok growth strategy in 2026 is to build topical authority while optimizing every video for retention and search intent.

Instead of posting random viral trends, creators should build a repeatable system.

### Step 1: Choose a Clear Niche

A niche helps TikTok understand your account and helps viewers know why they should follow you.

Examples of clear niches:

- TikTok growth for small businesses
- Shopify development tips
- AI tools for marketers
- Fitness for busy professionals
- Personal finance for beginners
- Web design tutorials

### Step 2: Build Content Pillars

Content pillars are recurring topic categories.

For a TikTok marketing account, content pillars might include:

| Content Pillar | Example Video |
|---|---|
| Algorithm education | How TikTok tests new videos |
| TikTok SEO | Where to put keywords in your TikTok videos |
| Analytics | How to read your retention graph |
| Content strategy | Why your hooks are not working |
| Monetization | How creators turn views into leads |

### Step 3: Create Search-Friendly Videos

Every video should answer a clear question or satisfy a clear viewer need.

Use this simple structure:

1. State the problem or promise
2. Explain the key idea
3. Give examples
4. Provide a practical takeaway
5. Ask a relevant engagement question

### Step 4: Review Analytics Weekly

TikTok analytics reveal what your audience actually responds to.

Track:

- Average watch time
- Completion rate
- Replays
- Saves
- Shares
- Follower conversion
- Traffic source
- Search queries
- Audience retention graph

### Step 5: Double Down on Winners

When a video performs well, do not simply celebrate it. Study it.

Ask:

- What was the hook?
- What topic did it cover?
- How long was it?
- What was the pacing?
- Did it get saves or shares?
- Did viewers comment with follow-up questions?
- Can this become a series?

Winning content should become a repeatable format.

## Common TikTok Algorithm Mistakes

Many creators struggle because they focus on the wrong things. The algorithm rewards viewer satisfaction, not shortcuts.

| Mistake | Why It Hurts | Better Approach |
|---|---|---|
| Weak hook | Users swipe away early | Start with a problem, promise, or result |
| Long intro | Reduces retention | Remove filler and begin immediately |
| Generic content | Hard to categorize | Make the topic specific |
| Keyword stuffing | Feels unnatural | Use keywords clearly but naturally |
| Too many hashtags | Looks unfocused | Use a few relevant hashtags |
| Chasing every trend | Weakens niche authority | Adapt trends only when relevant |
| Ignoring analytics | Repeats poor formats | Review retention and engagement weekly |
| Posting without a goal | Creates inconsistent results | Match each video to a clear intent |

## TikTok Algorithm Myths

### Myth 1: Followers Determine Reach

Follower count can help with credibility, but it does not guarantee reach. TikTok can distribute videos from small accounts if the content performs well.

### Myth 2: Hashtags Make Videos Viral

Hashtags help TikTok categorize content, but they do not make weak content go viral. Retention, watch time, saves, and shares are more important.

### Myth 3: Posting More Always Means More Growth

Posting frequently can help you learn faster, but poor-quality volume does not guarantee results. A focused posting schedule with strong content is better than random high-volume posting.

### Myth 4: Every View Drop Is a Shadow Ban

View drops are often caused by weaker content performance, audience mismatch, poor retention, or topic fatigue. A true restriction is less common than creators assume.

### Myth 5: You Must Use Trending Sounds

Trending sounds can help in some entertainment categories, but they are not required for growth. Educational, business, and tutorial content can perform well with original audio.

## Why TikTok Views Drop

A sudden drop in TikTok views can happen for several reasons.

| Cause | Explanation | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Lower retention | Viewers are leaving early | Improve hooks and pacing |
| Topic mismatch | Content is reaching the wrong audience | Clarify niche and keywords |
| Weak opening | Users swipe in the first seconds | Start with a stronger promise |
| Repetitive content | Audience loses interest | Add fresh examples and formats |
| Poor search clarity | TikTok cannot understand the topic | Use spoken keywords and captions |
| Trend fatigue | A format is overused | Create original angles |
| Inconsistent quality | Performance varies widely | Build a repeatable content process |

Before assuming a shadow ban, review retention, completion rate, traffic source, and recent content quality.

## How to Improve TikTok Watch Time

Watch time improves when users feel every second is worth watching.

Use these tactics:

### 1. Start with the Outcome

Tell viewers what they will gain.

Example:

Here are three TikTok ranking factors that matter more than hashtags.

### 2. Remove Filler

Avoid phrases like:

- Hey guys
- So basically
- I just wanted to come on here
- Before we get started

Start with value immediately.

### 3. Use Open Loops

An open loop creates curiosity.

Example:

Most creators optimize the wrong part of their video. The real problem is usually here.

### 4. Change Visuals

Use movement, text, cuts, screenshots, examples, or demonstrations to keep attention.

### 5. Make the Ending Valuable

A strong ending can increase completion rate and replays. End with a takeaway, checklist, or next step.

## How to Increase TikTok Saves and Shares

Saves and shares are high-value engagement signals. They show TikTok that a video has lasting value or social value.

### Content That Gets Saves

- Checklists
- Templates
- Tutorials
- Step-by-step guides
- Tool recommendations
- Mistake lists
- Strategy frameworks
- Definitions and explanations

### Content That Gets Shares

- Relatable problems
- Strong opinions
- Surprising facts
- Useful tips
- Funny situations
- Industry truths
- Content that helps a friend

A simple test: if your video could help someone later, it is save-worthy. If it could help someone else right now, it is share-worthy.

## TikTok Content Planning Table

Use this table to plan videos around search intent and engagement goals.

| Goal | Video Type | Example Hook | Best Engagement Signal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Get discovered | SEO tutorial | How TikTok SEO works in 2026 | Search traffic |
| Build trust | Case study | Here is why this video reached 500K views | Saves and follows |
| Start discussion | Opinion | Hashtags are not your growth problem | Comments |
| Drive shares | Relatable insight | Send this to a creator who posts every day but gets no views | Shares |
| Improve authority | Deep explanation | The real reason TikTok tests videos in stages | Watch time |
| Generate leads | Business advice | Businesses are using TikTok wrong in 2026 | Profile visits |

## Key Takeaways

- TikTok recommends videos based on user behavior, video information, and relevance signals.
- Watch time and completion rate are among the strongest ranking factors.
- Replays, shares, and saves show strong viewer satisfaction.
- TikTok SEO helps videos appear in search and topic-based discovery.
- Followers matter less than content performance.
- Hashtags help categorization but do not create virality by themselves.
- Topic authority improves long-term growth.
- Educational, tutorial, and problem-solving content can perform well in 2026.
- Sustainable growth comes from retention, intent, shares, and engagement.
- Creators should study analytics and repeat what works.

> **Ready to grow?** Learn more about algorithm changes in our [TikTok Algorithm 2026 trend analysis](/trends/tiktok-algorithm-2026-complete-guide) and optimize your website with our [free Website Audit](/tools/website-audit).

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How does the TikTok algorithm work in 2026?

The TikTok algorithm recommends videos based on watch time, completion rate, engagement, search relevance, user interests, and viewer satisfaction. It tests videos with relevant audiences and expands reach when performance signals are strong.

### What is the most important TikTok ranking factor?

Watch time and completion rate are among the most important TikTok ranking factors. If viewers stay engaged and finish the video, TikTok is more likely to distribute it to a larger audience.

### Do hashtags still matter on TikTok?

Yes, hashtags still matter, but they are not the main ranking factor. Hashtags help TikTok understand the topic of a video, but retention, watch time, saves, shares, and relevance are more important.

### Can small TikTok accounts go viral?

Yes. Small TikTok accounts can go viral because TikTok evaluates individual video performance. A new creator can reach a large audience if the video performs well with viewers.

### Does TikTok SEO help videos get more views?

Yes. TikTok SEO can help videos become more discoverable in search and recommendation systems. Using keywords in spoken audio, captions, on-screen text, and hashtags can improve topic clarity.

### How long does TikTok test a video?

TikTok testing time varies. Some videos gain reach quickly, while others grow over several days or weeks. Performance depends on retention, engagement, audience fit, and search relevance.

### Why are my TikTok views going down?

TikTok views may drop because of weak hooks, lower completion rate, poor audience fit, repetitive content, topic changes, or reduced engagement. A view drop does not always mean a shadow ban.

### Does posting time matter on TikTok?

Posting time can affect early engagement, especially if your audience is active at certain hours. However, content quality, retention, and relevance matter more than posting time alone.

### How often should I post on TikTok in 2026?

Consistency matters more than posting volume. Many creators benefit from posting several times per week, but the best schedule depends on content quality, niche, and available resources.

### Are likes important for the TikTok algorithm?

Likes are useful engagement signals, but they are usually weaker than watch time, completion rate, saves, shares, and meaningful comments.

### Can old TikTok videos go viral?

Yes. Old TikTok videos can gain new views through search, related recommendations, or renewed audience interest. Evergreen content has the best chance of long-term discovery.

### Should I delete low-performing TikTok videos?

Deleting low-performing videos is usually not necessary. Instead, review analytics and learn why the video underperformed. Occasional deletion is unlikely to define your account, but repeated deletion is not a growth strategy.

### What content performs best on TikTok in 2026?

Educational videos, tutorials, product reviews, storytelling, case studies, and entertaining content can all perform well. The best content type depends on the audience and niche.

### How many hashtags should I use on TikTok?

A good starting point is three to five relevant hashtags. Use hashtags that describe the topic, niche, and audience instead of unrelated trending tags.

### Does TikTok favor longer videos?

TikTok does not automatically favor longer videos. Longer videos can perform well if viewers stay engaged. Short videos can also perform strongly when completion rate and replays are high.

### What is a good TikTok hook?

A good TikTok hook gives viewers a reason to stop scrolling. It can introduce a problem, promise a result, challenge a belief, or create curiosity within the first few seconds.

### How do I increase TikTok completion rate?

To increase completion rate, remove slow intros, keep the video focused, use a clear structure, create curiosity, and deliver the promised value before the video ends.

### How do I get more saves on TikTok?

Create content with future value, such as tutorials, checklists, templates, step-by-step processes, tool lists, and strategy frameworks.

### How do I get more shares on TikTok?

Create content that is relatable, useful, surprising, funny, or helpful to a specific audience. People share videos when they believe someone else should see them.

### Is TikTok still good for business marketing in 2026?

Yes. TikTok can be valuable for businesses that create useful, entertaining, or educational content. It is especially powerful for awareness, product discovery, audience building, and trust-building.

# Developer Tools News June 2026: What's New This Month

June 2026 has been one of the busiest months for developer tools, AI coding assistants, cloud platforms, and productivity software. From major AI coding improvements to framework updates and infrastructure enhancements, developers now have more options than ever to build faster and work smarter.

In this monthly roundup, we break down the most important releases, explain what they mean for developers, and highlight the tools worth paying attention to.

> **Want the full list of AI tools developers actually use?** Check out our comprehensive guide: [20 AI Tools Every Developer Actually Uses (Not Just Hype)](/blog/ai-tools-developers-2026)

## Quick Summary

If you only have a few minutes, here are the biggest developer tool updates from June 2026:

| Category | Major Update | Impact |
|----------|-------------|--------|
| AI Coding | New reasoning models improve code generation accuracy | 40% faster coding workflows |
| Frameworks | Next.js ecosystem receives major performance improvements | 30% faster builds |
| Cloud Platforms | Deployment workflows become faster and cheaper | 50% reduction in CI/CD time |
| Developer Productivity | AI-powered debugging tools continue to evolve | 60% faster bug resolution |
| Security | New security scanning capabilities launched | Automated vulnerability detection |

author: DevelopersMatrix Editorial Team
content:
# ChatGPT vs Google AI Overview: Which Is Better for SEO in 2026?

Artificial intelligence is changing search faster than most website owners expected. Just two years ago, ranking on Google mainly depended on traditional SEO practices like backlinks, keywords, and content optimization. Today, AI generated answers are becoming the first thing users see before they even click a website.

This shift has created one of the biggest questions in digital marketing right now:

> Should businesses optimize for ChatGPT or focus on Google AI Overview?

The answer is not as simple as choosing one platform over the other. Both systems work differently, retrieve information differently, and reward different types of content.

In this guide, we will break down how ChatGPT and Google AI Overview work, what they mean for SEO, and which platform offers the biggest opportunity in 2026.

---

## What Is ChatGPT Search?

ChatGPT is no longer just a chatbot. It has evolved into a powerful information discovery system that millions of users now rely on for research, recommendations, learning, coding, and decision making.

Instead of showing ten blue links like traditional Google search, ChatGPT tries to give users direct answers in a conversational format.

For example, instead of searching:

`Best technical SEO tools`

Users now ask:

`What are the best technical SEO tools for a small business website?`

ChatGPT responds with summarized recommendations, explanations, and sometimes citations from websites it trusts.

This completely changes how users interact with information online.

If you want to improve your AI visibility and AI citation chances, tools like our [AI Prompt Library](https://developersmatrix.com/tools/ai-prompt-library) can help you create better structured prompts and AI optimized workflows.

---

## What Is Google AI Overview?

Google AI Overview is Google’s AI generated answer system integrated directly into search results.

When users search for certain topics, Google may display an AI summary above the traditional organic results.

These summaries pull information from multiple websites and combine them into one generated response.

Google AI Overview focuses heavily on:

- Trusted sources
- Topical authority
- EEAT signals
- Semantic relevance
- Helpful content
- Search intent

Unlike ChatGPT, Google still relies deeply on its traditional ranking systems and indexing infrastructure.

Website owners who want to understand how their site performs technically can use our [AI Website Audit Tool](https://developersmatrix.com/tools/website-audit) to identify technical SEO issues affecting visibility and crawlability.

---

## The Biggest Difference Between ChatGPT and Google AI Overview

The biggest difference is simple.

Google AI Overview is still built on top of Google Search.

ChatGPT behaves more like an AI research assistant.

Google wants to organize the web.

ChatGPT wants to answer questions directly.

That difference changes how websites get visibility.

---

## How ChatGPT Chooses Which Websites to Mention

ChatGPT tends to reference websites that provide:

- Clear explanations
- Structured content
- Unique insights
- Strong topical authority
- Original research
- Trustworthy information
- Semantic clarity

Content that performs well usually includes:

- Tutorials
- Comparisons
- Technical explanations
- FAQs
- Expert opinions
- Practical examples

Generic AI written blogs rarely get cited consistently.

ChatGPT prefers content that actually teaches something useful.

For example, highly detailed prompt engineering resources like our [ChatGPT Advanced Prompts 2026 Guide](https://developersmatrix.com/trends/chatgpt-advanced-prompts-2026) are more likely to perform well in AI retrieval systems because they provide practical and structured value.

---

## How Google AI Overview Selects Content

Google AI Overview is more connected to traditional SEO signals.

Google still evaluates:

- Backlinks
- Authority
- Crawlability
- Indexing
- EEAT
- Page experience
- Internal linking
- Structured data

However, AI Overview also rewards content that answers questions quickly and clearly.

Pages that rank well often include:

- Concise answers
- Semantic headings
- Question based sections
- High trust signals
- Expert formatting
- Updated information

---

## Which Platform Sends More Traffic?

This is where things become interesting.

Google AI Overview can reduce clicks because users often get answers directly on the search page.

ChatGPT works differently.

When ChatGPT references a website, users are usually deeper in the research stage. These users often have stronger intent and higher engagement.

Many publishers are starting to notice that AI referral traffic converts better than traditional search traffic.

Even though AI traffic is smaller right now, the quality is often higher.

---

## Why Most Websites Are Losing Visibility in AI Search

Most websites are still using old SEO strategies built only for Google rankings.

That approach is becoming outdated.

Many sites have problems like:

- Thin content
- Repetitive AI generated articles
- Weak EEAT
- Poor site architecture
- Low originality
- No entity authority
- Weak internal linking
- Poor content structure

AI systems are becoming extremely good at detecting low value content.

Websites that publish generic information without expertise are slowly disappearing from AI generated answers.

---

## What Type of Content Performs Best in AI Search?

The websites winning in AI search usually publish content that feels genuinely useful.

The best performing formats include:

### Comparison Articles

Examples:

- ChatGPT vs Gemini
- Ahrefs vs SEMrush
- React vs Next.js

Comparison content works because users want direct decision making help.

---

### Original Research

AI systems love unique data.

Examples:

- SEO studies
- Benchmark reports
- Tool testing
- Industry statistics

This type of content is highly citation worthy.

---

### Step by Step Guides

Detailed implementation focused tutorials perform extremely well because they provide practical value.

Users and AI systems both prefer content that solves problems clearly.

---

### Expert Opinion Content

AI systems prioritize content with real expertise.

Experience matters more now than ever before.

---

## Is Traditional SEO Still Important?

Yes. Absolutely.

Technical SEO still matters heavily.

Without proper indexing and crawlability, AI systems may never understand your content properly.

Important technical SEO factors include:

- Clean site structure
- Internal linking
- Schema markup
- Page speed
- Mobile optimization
- Canonical optimization
- XML sitemaps
- Semantic HTML
- Rendering accessibility

AI search is not replacing technical SEO.

It is expanding it.

If you want to identify hidden technical SEO issues on your own website, our [AI Website Audit Tool](https://developersmatrix.com/tools/website-audit) can help uncover problems related to performance, indexing, metadata, and crawlability.

---

## Why EEAT Matters More in 2026

Google and AI systems both want trustworthy information.

This is why EEAT has become critical.

EEAT stands for:

- Experience
- Expertise
- Authoritativeness
- Trustworthiness

Websites without clear expertise signals struggle to gain AI visibility.

Important EEAT improvements include:

- Real author pages
- Company information
- Editorial standards
- Updated content
- Expert reviews
- Transparent policies
- Trustworthy branding

Anonymous content websites are becoming less effective every year.

---

## Which Is Better for SEO in 2026?

The real answer is this:

> You should optimize for both.

Focusing only on Google rankings is risky now.

Focusing only on AI visibility is also risky.

The best strategy is building a website that:

- Answers questions clearly
- Demonstrates expertise
- Has strong technical SEO
- Creates original value
- Structures information properly
- Builds topical authority

That approach works across both traditional search and AI search systems.

---

## The Future of SEO Is GEO

A new concept called GEO is becoming increasingly important.

GEO stands for Generative Engine Optimization.

Instead of optimizing only for rankings, GEO focuses on optimizing for:

- AI retrieval
- AI citations
- Semantic understanding
- Entity recognition
- Answer generation

This is likely the future direction of modern SEO.

Websites that adapt early will have a major advantage over competitors.

Learning advanced prompting techniques is also becoming important for GEO. Resources like our [AI Prompt Library](https://developersmatrix.com/tools/ai-prompt-library) and [ChatGPT Advanced Prompts 2026 Guide](https://developersmatrix.com/trends/chatgpt-advanced-prompts-2026) can help businesses understand how AI systems interpret and generate information.

---

## Final Thoughts

The SEO industry is entering a major transition period.

Google AI Overview and ChatGPT are changing how people discover information online.

The websites that succeed in 2026 will not be the ones publishing the most content.

They will be the ones creating the most useful content.

Strong technical SEO, real expertise, topical authority, and original insights are becoming more important than ever.

If your website focuses on genuine value instead of mass producing generic articles, you will have a much better chance of gaining visibility across both Google Search and AI powered search systems.

The future belongs to websites that humans trust and AI systems understand.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Does ChatGPT affect Google SEO rankings?

ChatGPT itself does not directly affect Google rankings, but AI search behavior is changing how users discover websites. Websites optimized for AI retrieval and helpful content are more likely to perform well across both systems.

### What is GEO in SEO?

GEO stands for Generative Engine Optimization. It focuses on optimizing content for AI powered search systems like ChatGPT, Google AI Overview, Perplexity, and Bing Copilot.

### How do websites get cited in ChatGPT?

Websites usually get cited when they provide structured, trustworthy, original, and highly useful information with strong topical authority and semantic clarity.

### Is traditional SEO still important in 2026?

Yes. Technical SEO, backlinks, EEAT, site structure, and indexing still play a major role in visibility across both Google Search and AI search systems.

### What type of content works best for AI search?

Comparison articles, original research, expert tutorials, technical guides, statistics, and practical implementation focused content tend to perform best in AI search systems.
